name: Acarbose
route_note: oral tablet taken with the first bite of each main meal

discovery.note: A pseudo-tetrasaccharide produced by fermentation of Actinoplanes bacteria, found in Bayer's screen for carbohydrate-digestion inhibitors.

tagline: A bacterial sugar mimic that slows carbohydrate digestion in the gut
summary: Acarbose is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that delays digestion of complex carbohydrates in the small intestine, blunting the rise in blood glucose after meals. It is widely used in China and parts of Asia; flatulence and bloating limit its use elsewhere.
mechanism: Acarbose is a complex oligosaccharide that competitively and reversibly inhibits brush-border alpha-glucosidases (sucrase, maltase, glucoamylase, isomaltase) and pancreatic alpha-amylase. Starches and disaccharides are therefore broken down into absorbable monosaccharides more slowly and further along the intestine.

This flattens post-prandial glucose and insulin peaks. Undigested carbohydrate reaching the colon is fermented by bacteria, producing gas and the drug's typical gastrointestinal side effects. Very little acarbose is absorbed.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, as adjunct to diet, alone or with other agents
Prevention of type 2 diabetes in impaired glucose tolerance (some countries)

history.title: Discovery published
history.detail: Bayer scientists led by Delf Schmidt describe alpha-glucosidase inhibitors of microbial origin, including acarbose.

history.title: STOP-NIDDM
history.detail: STOP-NIDDM shows acarbose reduces progression from impaired glucose tolerance to diabetes (Lancet 2002).

history.title: ACE trial
history.detail: The Acarbose Cardiovascular Evaluation in 6,522 Chinese patients with coronary disease finds no reduction in major cardiovascular events but less new diabetes.

pk.metabolism: degraded in the gut by bacteria and digestive enzymes

facts: Hypoglycaemia during acarbose combination therapy should be treated with glucose (dextrose), not sucrose, because sucrose digestion is inhibited.
Acarbose is produced by fermentation of Actinoplanes bacteria.

references.title: Holman RR et al. Acarbose Cardiovascular Evaluation (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2017)
